skill.name: set-up-shopify-google-ads-ltv-bidding
skill.description: Set up customer lifetime value bidding for a Shopify store in Google Ads through Product Metrics. Check tracking and consent, choose a revenue or profit conversion action, and verify that eligible orders reach the action.
skill.summary: Configure and verify Shopify lifetime value bidding in Google Ads with Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most flags are Markdown formatting, documentation links, or normal conversion tracking, not shell substitution or host reconnaissance. The workflow does allow authenticated vendor operations and recommends an unpinned installer. The review also found out-of-scope integration and credential instructions and insufficient safeguards for order data and browser handoffs.

remediation.suggestion: Document a verified installer version and immutable repository revision. Ask the operator to approve installation before running downloaded code.

remediation.issue: Authenticated writes lack a general approval step
remediation.suggestion: Show the selected account, operation, affected data, and proposed changes before writing. Request approval and keep the default access read-only.

remediation.issue: Setup can expand beyond the requested ad channel
remediation.suggestion: Limit the prerequisite checklist to Shopify and Google Ads. Before authorizing Product Metrics, show the operator the data, recipients, permissions, and charges.

remediation.issue: Credential exceptions ask for unrelated secrets
remediation.suggestion: Remove the credential exceptions from this skill. Use the official account authorization screens and never pass secrets in command arguments.

remediation.issue: Order lookups can expose unnecessary customer or order data
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the store before querying. Use a test order or request only the needed fields, and omit identifiers and contact details from replies.

remediation.issue: Browser handoffs trust URLs returned by the integration
remediation.suggestion: Check returned URLs against expected HTTPS origins for the setup step. For unexpected origins, direct the operator to the official account interface.

content.user_title: Set Up Shopify LTV Bidding in Google Ads
content.value_statement: A first purchase does not show what a repeat customer spends over time. Use Product Metrics to verify Shopify lifetime value signals and choose a Google Ads bidding goal.
actual_capabilities: Check what is already configured in a connected Product Metrics workspace.
Guide Shopify, Google Ads, and Merchant Center setup for server-side tracking.
Check the configured consent banner and verify that a paid test order reached Product Metrics.
Explain when to choose Revenue LTV or Profit LTV and how missing costs affect Profit LTV.
Guide the operator through selecting one primary purchase action and verify its status afterward.
limitations: Live checks require authorized Product Metrics access. The operator handles approvals in Shopify and Google Ads.
Lifetime value covers observed orders for each connected store. It does not predict future purchases or import orders from before connection.
Google Ads receives LTV conversions only for recognized customers with analytics consent, ad user data consent, and matchable contact information.
Profit LTV requires known order costs. Missing costs can leave only a revenue signal.

use_cases.title: Check whether a store is ready
use_cases.description: Find which connections, permissions, and consent settings are missing before setting up lifetime value bidding.

use_cases.title: Plan a one-campaign bidding trial
use_cases.description: Compare Revenue LTV and Profit LTV, then plan which conversion action to make primary for one campaign.

use_cases.title: Investigate a missing Profit LTV signal
use_cases.description: Use a paid test order to check whether recognition, consent, or missing costs could explain a missing conversion.

prompt_templates.title: Explain lifetime value bidding
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain Revenue LTV and Profit LTV for Shopify in Google Ads. Tell me what I need before I can use either one.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Compare the two signals before connecting accounts.

prompt_templates.title: Check setup readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check setup for [store] and [Google Ads account] in Product Metrics. Use read-only checks and list anything missing. Do not connect any other channels.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: Review a store that already has a Product Metrics workspace.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a paid test order
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my paid test order reached Product Metrics. Report any visible recognition or cost issue, and tell me how to check consent. Do not show customer details.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Diagnose tracking after placing a test order.

prompt_templates.title: Plan and verify a bidding trial
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a one-campaign switch to Revenue LTV or Profit LTV for [campaign]. Explain the target ROAS tradeoffs and tell me which goal settings to change. Wait for my confirmation, then verify the goal status without making changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Change one campaign after validating tracking and costs.

output_examples.input: Can I start testing Revenue LTV for this store?
output: Shopify, Google Ads, and Merchant Center are connected.
The Revenue LTV action exists and is secondary. Your current primary action is unchanged.
Place a paid test order with the required consent before switching the campaign goal.

output_examples.input: Why did my test order show revenue but no profit?
output: Product Metrics received the paid test order and recognized the customer.
The order has an unknown cost, so it is not eligible for Profit LTV.
Review the variant cost in Shopify and any applicable fees under Profit tracking in Product Metrics.

best_practices: Confirm the store and Google Ads client account before connecting services or changing conversion settings.
Verify the consent banner and use a paid test order before changing campaign goals.
Start with one campaign, keep one purchase action primary for it, and choose a target ROAS for the new value signal.
anti_patterns: Making Revenue LTV and Profit LTV primary for the same campaign.
Copying the old purchase target ROAS without accounting for differences in eligible orders and conversion values.
Connecting unrelated ad channels or including customer contact details in verification reports.

faq.question: Does this predict customer lifetime value?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics uses observed paid orders, and each eligible conversion carries what that order adds.

faq.question: Does Product Metrics import earlier Shopify orders?
faq.answer: No. Each store starts accumulating lifetime value from the orders Product Metrics sees after connection.

faq.question: What is required for Google Ads to receive an LTV conversion?
faq.answer: The customer must be recognized, and the visitor must grant analytics and ad user data consent. The order also needs matchable contact information.

faq.question: Why might I see Revenue LTV but no Profit LTV?
faq.answer: Revenue LTV does not need cost data. Profit LTV is sent only when the order's costs are known.

faq.question: Will the skill change my primary purchase goal?
faq.answer: No. You change the goal in Google Ads. The assistant can guide the change and check its status afterward.

faq.question: What access do I need to set it up?
faq.answer: You need workspace admin access in Product Metrics. You also need Shopify app and theme permissions, plus access to Google Ads and linked Merchant Center.
